newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Glorious Sun continues strong advance.
newsitem.headline: Glorious Sun continues strong advance.

text.p: Glorious Sun Enterprises shares rose over 20 percent on Monday morning to hit a peak of HK$4.85, its highest level since its IPO, on renewed interest in issues with exposure to consumer spending in China, brokers said.
"Interest (in the company) is induced by the China concept," said Francis Wu, institutional sales manager at South China Securities.

Glorious Sun, a casual wear manufacturer and retailer, offered 100 million shares to the public and 150 million in a placement in mid-September at HK$1.60 per share. The retail portion of the issue was 236 times subscribed.

The stock ended the Monday morning session up HK$0.725 at HK$4.575 after rising to HK$4.85. The share has risen steadily since its listing on the back of expectations of an upturn in consumer spending in China.

"With sustained strong income growth over the past two years and with a falling trend in interest rates, we are forecasting a consumption-led recovery (in the economy) to unfold in coming months," said Nicholas Kwan, senior economist at Merrill Lynch.
Glorious Sun had 203 shops in China at the time of listing and planned to raise the number to 330 by April 1998.
"The company's stores are mainly located in the north and it will try to tap the market in southern China in the coming two years," said Kathleen Emerson, analyst at DBS Securities.
She said the share was offered on a price/earnings ratio of 9.2 times 1997 forecast earnings per share of HK$0.175.
Some brokers said the share was now quite expensive.

"I wouldn't advise clients to get into it at this price unless there is a clearer picture of what is going on in next two years," said Sean Li, associate director at Amsteel Securities. "For those who like the concept, Goldlion and Chaifa are cheaper," Li added.
